correctness.rationale: For adjacent exceptional positive bonds a,b>1 of a half-line weighted unilateral shift, unitary phase conjugation gives w(S)=sup sigma(S+S*)/2. Essential spectrum of the finite-rank perturbed free Jacobi matrix is [-2,2]. At lambda>2 the left Dirichlet polynomial ratio p_(k-1)/p_k and right decaying root t=(lambda-sqrt(lambda²-4))/2 produce the exact bound-state condition F_k=lambda-a² p_(k-1)/p_k-b²t=0. It strictly increases with lambda; F_k(2+)=2-[k/(k+1)]a²-b² yields if-and-only-if threshold and explains edge resonance at equality. Ratio p_(k-1)/p_k increases with k, giving nondecreasing radii (strict when next >1). Its t-expression tends to t; G=lambda-(a²+b²)t has root lambda*=sqrt(s)+1/sqrt(s), s=a²+b²-1, G_prime(lambda*)=2s/(s-1). The mean-value theorem on the exponentially small remaining term gives lim s^(k+1/2)(r∞-r_k)=a²(s-1)²/(4s²). Independently verified k=1 a=b=5/3 root 5/2, three finite location scans and two asymptotic coefficients; general proof uses exact recurrence.
residual_risks: Fixed a,b>1, adjacent defects, complex Hilbert half-line only; no uniform weak-defect asymptotic.
Exact edge equality is not an l2 eigenvector, and computational bracketing does not establish nonexistence.
